Represent ORC during client meetings, public meetings, industry conferences, and executive-level presentations. Has the ability to lead and develop high-performing teams while fostering accountability and collaboration. Thinks strategically and can balance long-term program goals with day-to-day operational needs. Is comfortable making informed business decisions using financial and operational data. Demonstrates exceptional organization and planning skills while managing multiple priorities. Has excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills. Thrives in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Is committed to delivering exceptional customer service and continuous improvement. Minimum Requirements Minimum of [8] years of right of way experience, including leadership across multiple projects Working with or within a Department of Transportation Minimum of three (3) years managing complex transportation infrastructure programs or projects. Minimum of three (3) years leading Project Managers and multidisciplinary teams. Prior experience directing project managers or large delivery teams Proficient with MS Office Suite — specifically Excel, Word, and Outlook An iOS or Android smartphone to access ORC’s systems Valid driver’s license Bonus Points if You Have Bachelor's degree. Previous experience serving as a Program Manager or Project Manager on TDOT consultant contracts. Established relationships with TDOT leadership and transportation stakeholders. Experience supporting Design-Build or alternative delivery transportation programs. Every candidate is assessed and evaluated during the hiring process to determine their level based on factors, such as training, transferable skills, work experience, business needs, and market demands. Your offer will reflect the level that best matches your experience. Relocation and per diem are not provided. Ready to Apply? Make your mark on projects that matter. Apply now to join a supportive team that invests in your future. Employees must avoid any relationship or activity that might impair, or even appear to impair, their ability to make objective and fair decisions when performing their jobs. To avoid conflicts of interest, employees are prohibited from performing any services for clients or perceived clients during nonworking time that are normally performed by ORC, including the sale of real estate. Physical Requirements: While performing the duties of this job, it requires a combination of office-based and field work. Employees will spend prolonged periods sitting and performing computer-based tasks, including typing, data entry, and virtual communication, while also regularly traveling to landowner properties, project sites, and government facilities, some of which may be in rural or remote locations with limited accessibility. Fieldwork may require walking over uneven terrain, standing, or navigating outdoor environments, with routine exposure to varying weather conditions such as heat, cold, rain, and snow. The role also involves frequent interaction with a diverse range of individuals, including landowners, government officials, and members of the public, requiring the ability to communicate effectively and maintain professionalism across differing personalities and potentially challenging situations.
